title: STS2CharacterPackage
description: The full definition of a custom Slay the Spire 2 character. This is the ONLY thing that lives in the browser (localStorage). Nothing server-side ever persists it — it is sent to /api/compile on export and discarded by the server after the response is returned.

formatVersion.description: Bump whenever the schema changes shape, so the frontend can migrate old localStorage blobs.

author.description: Credited as the mod's author in the generated manifest. Optional — defaults to 'Unknown' at compile time if omitted.

modVersion.description: Semantic version string for the exported mod, e.g. '1.0.0'. Optional — defaults to '1.0.0' at compile time.

id.description: Slug used as the C# namespace / mod id, e.g. 'ember_knight'

energyPerTurn.description: [Round 95, VERIFIED compiled as of this round via decompiling TheBurdenedNewCharacter.dll's real TheBurdened.cs — public override int MaxEnergy, same override-block position as StartingHp/StartingGold] Compiles to `public override int MaxEnergy => <value>;` on the generated character class (Character.cs.template) — previously collected but left uncompiled ("nowhere confirmed to put it").

baseOrbSlotCount.description: [Round 95, Tyler: "'Char options for orb slots base' is an option for how many orb slots the character should start with. The Defect (base game character) starts with like 3 orb slots."] [BEST EFFORT via decompiling TheBurdenedNewCharacter.dll's real TheBurdened.cs — `public override int BaseOrbSlotCount => 0;`, same override-block position as StartingHp/StartingGold/MaxEnergy above] Compiles to `public override int BaseOrbSlotCount => <value>;` on the generated character class. Defaults to 0 when omitted (a safe no-orbs default) — set this above 0 for an Orb-focused character (see the `orbs` array below for the Orb definitions themselves).

startingDeckCardIds.description: Card ids in the starting deck. Not deduplicated — a card id may appear more than once, and how many times it appears IS its starting-deck quantity (e.g. 5 copies of a Strike's id = 5 starting Strikes). This is a direct consequence of how backend/compiler.js emits StartingDeck: each entry maps 1:1 to its own `ModelDb.Card<T>()` expression with no dedup, so N copies of an id really do produce N separate starting-deck instances. The frontend's card board Quantities dropdown is what edits this field to more than one copy per card.

startingRelicId.description: LEGACY, superseded by startingRelicIds (array) below as of the multi-starter-relic round. Kept only so a project saved before that round still loads — the frontend migrates this into startingRelicIds[] on load and no longer writes to this field. backend/compiler.js still reads it as a fallback for old saved packages that reach generateProject() directly without going through the frontend's migration pass.

startingRelicIds.description: [VERIFIED via real sts2.dll IL disassembly, 2026-09-01 — see TOOLCHAIN_FINDINGS.md "character-select click crash #3"] CharacterModel.StartingRelics is a real IReadOnlyList<RelicModel> — genuinely a list, not capped at one entry (NCharacterSelectScreen.SelectCharacter() only ever unconditionally reads index [0], which is why a NON-EMPTY list was the original hard requirement, but nothing caps it above 1). Relic ids here, in order, become this character's StartingRelics. Resolution order (backend/compiler.js): this array if non-empty, else the legacy singular startingRelicId if set, else every relics[] entry with rarity "Starter".

gender.description: Maps to the real MegaCrit.Sts2.Core.Entities.Characters.CharacterGender enum [VERIFIED via reflect-baselib rounds 11/12] — an abstract, override-required member on CharacterModel/CustomCharacterModel. Optional; defaults to Neutral when omitted (for backward-compat with characters saved before this field existed).

branch.description: Free-text note of which STS2 Steam branch (e.g. 'default', 'beta') this character package targets. Not compiled or validated — a reminder to Tyler only, since BaseLib's shape can differ between branches.

resourceBarAnchor.description: [LEGACY, round 92/53 — superseded by the per-entry resourceBars[].anchor field below as of round 101] A single character-wide anchor for every resource bar. Kept only as a fallback: a resourceBars[] entry with no anchor of its own resolves to this value, so a project saved before round 101 keeps behaving exactly as it did. New/edited bars should set their own resourceBars[].anchor instead — Tyler: "the 'Resource bars anchor' section. Can we move that to the status section. Ideally i'd like to be able to set that per status." See backend/compiler.js's resolveBarAnchor()/writeResourceBars() and claude/round92-resource-bars.md.

resourceBars.description: [BEST EFFORT — first real build of this feature] Each entry is an on-screen bar tied to a status/mechanic's real current stack count (ForgeActions.GetStatusStacks<T>, the same [VERIFIED] generic amountScalesWithStatus already uses), generalizing the bar-drawing shape already proven real in Tyler's own installed mod (TheBurdenedNewCharacter's Patches.ModStatusBarsPatch, round 51/52 evidence) into a schema-driven Forge feature. Optional; an omitted/empty array compiles to nothing (no Generated/ForgeResourceBar*.cs at all). Round 101 — each entry picks its own anchor (see the `anchor` property below), so different bars can anchor to different places on the same character; up to 3 standalone bars are supported PER anchor (not 3 total across both), and the "below health bar" anchor supports only 1 bar/diamond group total — see backend/compiler.js's writeResourceBars() for the exact per-anchor caps.

enabled.description: Set false to keep the bar's configuration without compiling it in — mirrors how other optional entries in this schema stay editable while disabled.

anchor.description: Round 101 — where THIS bar anchors on screen, independent of every other entry. "EnergyCounter" sits above the energy counter (up to 3 standalone bars there); "HealthBar" sits below the health bar (1 bar/diamond group total there, and is the default — round 102, Tyler: "they should all go below the health bar by default"), with an explicit Creature.IsPlayer + character-type guard so it doesn't draw under enemy health bars too. Optional; an entry with no anchor of its own falls back to the character-wide resourceBarAnchor (above), then to "HealthBar" — see backend/compiler.js's resolveBarAnchor(). Every entry sharing one diamondGroup must resolve to the same anchor (a diamond group is one indivisible widget). Round 102 — the Forge UI only lets a mechanic-linked ("custom") bar's own per-status editor move this away from the default; the Character panel's bar list has no anchor control at all.

label.description: Optional display label on the bar itself. Defaults to the chosen status's own name when omitted.

statusKind.description: Same 3-field vocabulary as amountScalesWithStatus/amountScalesWithBuiltinStatus elsewhere in this schema — whether the tracked status is one of this character's own mechanics ("custom") or a real built-in game status ("vanilla").

status.description: Mechanic id — used when statusKind is "custom" (or omitted).

builtinStatus.description: Real built-in status name (see BUILTIN_STATUSES) — used when statusKind is "vanilla".

max.description: The stack count at which this bar reads as full.

color.description: Hex color for the bar's fill, e.g. "#3399ff".

layout.description: Round 94 — "standalone" (default) is an independent bar, same as round 92's original shape. "diamond" reproduces Tyler's own real, shipping, hand-built ModStatusBarsPatch layout exactly [VERIFIED — reverse-engineered from Tyler's own installed TheBurdenedNewCharacter.dll v3.0.0, then further hardened through rounds 93/94's tooltip fixes on that same real code]: two side bars flanking a center diamond, sharing one combined widget. Diamond-layout entries need diamondGroup + diamondRole below to say which 3 (or 2) bars belong to the same widget and where each sits.

diamondGroup.description: Only used when layout is "diamond" — an arbitrary id shared by the 2-3 entries that make up one dual-bar+diamond widget. Entries with different diamondGroup values compile into separate widgets.

diamondRole.description: Only used when layout is "diamond" — which position this entry fills in its diamondGroup. Exactly one "left" and one "right" are required per group; "center" is optional (a group with only left+right is two bars with no diamond between them).

bodySpriteAssetRef.description: [EXPORTED into the compiled mod as of the 'fully functional' round — BEST EFFORT confidence] asset id, see assets[] (kind:'bodySprite'), exactly 512×512px. combatSpriteScale.description: [Round 122, Tyler: "is it possible to add a slider to change the size of the sprite?"] Uniform size multiplier for the character's on-screen combat sprite — 1 = the existing auto-normalized default size (a Body sprite or pose-sheet idle frame is scaled to fill the standard ~465px-tall creature bounds, same as every base-game creature), 0.5 = half that size, 2 = double. Applies to BOTH the pose-sheet AnimationPlayer system (character.poseSheets) and the legacy static single-image creature_visuals scene — whichever one is actually generated for this character (see compiler.js's writeCharacterArt/generatePoseSheetVisuals). The Bounds/CenterPos/IntentPos/OrbPos/TalkPos marker node offsets scale proportionally too, so hover/click bounds, the intent icon, and the energy-orb-channel VFX position all stay visually aligned with the resized sprite rather than the sprite alone changing size. Baked into the generated C#/scene at compile time as a plain multiplier on the existing fixed numbers — no new runtime mechanism, same "generate the final numbers once" convention as every other Forge-computed value.

poseSheets.description: [Round 121 — the 'Advanced' character/art sub-section Tyler scoped in round 95: "There should be an option to add a sprite sheet for every possible pose in the game. If I attack, I should be able to upload a sprite sheet that shows a full attack animation. The FPS should be customizable, and the frame count should allow for as little as 1."] Seven named poses, each an optional sprite-sheet animation (see poseSheetEntry below), each fully independent — Tyler, round 121 follow-up: "Lets just replace the idle sprite with the sprite sheet if they upload one. The other spritesheets should be ignored unless something is uploaded to them." Uploading idle simply replaces the character's resting look/animation (in place of the static Body sprite); every other pose is used only if its own sheet is uploaded, and is otherwise silently skipped — there is no dependency between poses any more. Uploading NO pose sheets at all leaves the character exactly as before (static Body sprite, no AnimationPlayer, no ShouldReceiveCombatHooks-driven overrides) — fully backward compatible. Uploading ANY pose sheet (idle or not) switches CreateCustomVisuals() (backend/compiler.js's generatePoseSheetVisuals()) to a real Godot AnimationPlayer/AnimationLibrary that frame-slices each uploaded sheet via AtlasTexture, mirroring Tyler's own hand-built, real, compiled-and-tested reference implementation in TheBurdenedNewCharacter's Characters/TheBurdened.cs (idle + attack poses, 50/7 frames respectively, 9 FPS — found via the device bridge, round 121). The resting/base look is resolved in priority order: the idle sheet if uploaded; else the existing Body sprite (bodySpriteAssetRef), exported and loaded as a plain static texture same as it always was; else, if neither is set but some other pose sheet is, that pose sheet's own first frame ([BEST EFFORT] fallback for the rare case of a character with no idle and no Body sprite at all). Each of the six non-idle poses (attack/heavyAttack/cast/hurt/death/victory) compiles to a real hook override on the generated character class (CharacterModel already extends AbstractModel and already has ShouldReceiveCombatHooks => true unconditionally — Character.cs.template) that reaches the live combat Creature straight off the hook's own parameter, navigates Creature.GetCreatureNode() (real, public, [VERIFIED via direct sts2.dll IL read, round 121]) -> NCreature.Visuals (real, public) -> the AnimationPlayer this same CreateCustomVisuals() call built, and plays that pose's animation if uploaded (HasAnimation guard — an un-uploaded pose is simply skipped, the character stays on whatever it was already playing). attack/heavyAttack/cast dispatch off AfterCardPlayed (CardType.Attack vs Skill/Power, heavyAttack further gated on the played card implementing the new IHeavyAttackCard marker — see card.advancedOptions.heavyAttackAnimation); hurt off AfterDamageReceived; death off BeforeDeath (stays on its last frame, does not auto-return to idle); victory off AfterCombatVictory (no Creature param on that real hook — resolved via room.CombatState.Players.FirstOrDefault().Creature, a real, already-established single-player-safe fallback pattern used elsewhere in this codebase for hooks with no bound Creature). When idle itself isn't uploaded, a non-held pose finishing returns the sprite to the resolved resting texture directly (Body sprite or fallback pose frame) rather than trying to play a nonexistent "idle" animation. [VERIFIED via direct sts2.dll/BaseLib.dll IL read, round 121 — Creature.GetCreatureNode(), NCreature.Visuals, CombatRoom.CombatState, CharacterModel/AbstractModel's real AfterCardPlayed/AfterDamageReceived/BeforeDeath/AfterCombatVictory virtuals, and CustomCharacterModel.CreateCustomVisuals() as a real override point already proven working by Tyler's own compiled TheBurdened.cs] NCreature.SetAnimationTrigger (the base game's own animation-trigger mechanism) was also checked and confirmed Spine-only (a no-op whenever _spineAnimator is null, which it always is for a plain-Sprite2D character) — this is why pose triggering is driven directly rather than relying on any base-game auto-trigger.

chronicles.description: [Round 203, replaces the old DESIGN-TIME-PREVIEW-ONLY lore[] field — Tyler: "change the name of lore to 'Chronicles'. Chronicles are a collection of items called 'Epochs'."] [VERIFIED real, compiled, ENFORCED game mechanic — MegaCrit.Sts2.Core.Timeline.StoryModel/EpochModel, confirmed via direct sts2.dll IL disassembly and by decompiling Tyler's own updated TheBurdenedNewCharacter.dll v3.] A Chronicle (StoryModel) is a named group of Epochs shown together on the character's timeline; see #/definitions/chronicle and #/definitions/epoch.

orb.description: The character's energy/HP orb ART config — NOT a gameplay Orb (see the top-level `orbs` array for those). [VERIFIED, EXPORTED into the compiled mod as of the 'fully functional' round, UNLESS mode is 'default' (Ironclad default) — there's no real art configured in that mode, so nothing is exported and no override is added, matching the live preview showing nothing too.] When exported, all 5 layers (bundled default art, or a custom upload per-layer) are written to pack/images/packed/energy_counters/<id>_layer_{1..5}.png and wired via the real EnergyCounterLayerPath/CustomEnergyCounter overrides (BaseLib.Abstracts.CustomEnergyCounter, confirmed shape: a Func<int,string> + 2 Godot.Color args; the override's return type is `CustomEnergyCounter?`, nullable — CS1715, a real build error Tyler hit on his first real dotnet build, fixed 2026-08-27) — confirmed via IL disassembly of Tyler's own compiled TheBurdenedNewCharacter.dll. The 2 Color arguments' real meaning is unconfirmed [BEST EFFORT], both currently default to character.color.

mode.description: New characters default to 'customLayers' with layers[] pre-seeded to {assetRef:null, color:null} × 5 — i.e. every layer just shows Forge's bundled default placeholder art (ORB_LAYER_DEFAULT_ASSETS in frontend/index.html: Background/SpinA/SpinB/Middle/Front.png) with no tint, so a brand-new character's orb preview looks like Tyler's own Complete.png reference out of the box. These are REAL placeholder art Tyler uploaded directly ("Those are all placeholder images that should be overlayed on top of each other to make the energy icon"), replacing the previous color-only gradient approximation (IRONCLAD_PLACEHOLDER_LAYER_COLORS, now removed) that rendered 5 shrinking concentric circles instead of real per-layer shapes. The LAYER COUNT of 5 is CONFIRMED real (not a Forge guess) — verified via direct IL/metadata disassembly of Tyler's own TheBurdenedNewCharacter.dll and BaseLib.dll: BaseLib.Utils.NodeFactories.NEnergyCounterFactory.FromLegacy calls CustomEnergyCounter.LayerImagePath(i) exactly 5 times with literal 1-based indices 1-5, the only call site in either assembly. The per-layer ROLE mapping is confirmed too, from Tyler's own Layers.png reference tool: Background (outer shell/backdrop), Spin A/Spin B (2 independently-rotating elements), Middle (glow behind the number), Front (thin legibility plate behind the number). Spin A and Spin B now actually animate in the live preview — Tyler: "If we really want spinA and spinB to spin in the app, that is fine, but spinB needs to spin at about half the speed of spinA" — implemented as plain CSS rotation, Spin B's animation-duration exactly double Spin A's (see .orb-layer-spin-a/-spin-b in frontend/index.html). A rotation re-test on real in-game screenshots (TestEnergy1/2/3.png) still couldn't measure real rotation speed/direction from footage (inconclusive — see TOOLCHAIN_FINDINGS.md), so the exact real-world spin rate is still unknown; the 2x ratio is the one concrete data point Tyler gave directly. 'buildFromColor' also renders the same 5 bundled layer images (not a flat fill) but auto-derives each layer's tint from `character.color` via CSS-mask + HSL lightness shift (see autoLayerColors/autoMiddleGradient/shiftLightness in frontend/index.html), nothing stored on the character beyond `color` itself — Tyler: "Build from colors should default to showing the placeholder energy that we created, but color shift each layer to be based off of their selected color. The Background should ideally attempt to be the color they have selected, with spinA being lighter, spin B being somewhere between the background and spinA, Middle should be a combination of dark and light highlights, and front should be darker than the background." Implemented exactly: Background = character.color as-is; Spin A = +26 lightness; Spin B = +13 lightness (between Background and Spin A); Front = -22 lightness (darker); Middle can't be a single flat tint since it needs BOTH a dark and a light highlight at once, so it's rendered as a radial-gradient mask instead (light highlight near one edge, base color in the middle, dark highlight opposite) — an interpretation call, flagged to Tyler, since "a combination of dark and light highlights" doesn't map to one CSS color. Spin A/Spin B still animate at the same 2x ratio in this mode. 'default' (Use Ironclad default) hides the ENTIRE preview row (badge + Show-stars checkbox) rather than showing anything — Tyler: "if 'use ironclad default' is selected, don't bother showing the preview", since Forge has no real Ironclad default art to show. See TOOLCHAIN_FINDINGS.md for the full trail.

layers.description: 5 layer rows, numbered 1-5 by the real engine's LayerImagePath(1..5) call order — NOT their paint order. CORRECTED in Round 119 via full IL disassembly of BaseLib's NEnergyCounterFactory::FromLegacy/AddLayer against Tyler's own updated TheBurdenedNewCharacter.dll: the real bottom-to-top composite order is Backdrop (see orb.backdropAssetRef, a separate mechanism) → Layer 2 (Spin A) → Layer 3 (Spin B) → Layer 1 → Layer 4 (Middle) → Layer 5 (Front). Layer 1 therefore paints OVER the two spin layers, not below them as previously assumed — its bundled default was changed from an opaque shape to a blank/transparent placeholder so it no longer hides Spin A/B by default. Each row independently combines an image (bundled default or custom upload) with an optional flat color tint — Tyler: "I want the user to be able to change the colors of each layer, but to still be able to replace each layer with their own image and see what it looks like in real-time." Replaces the old {mode:'color'|'image', color, assetRef} shape (formatVersion 8->9 migration in frontend/index.html) where color/image used to be mutually exclusive via a mode toggle — now both apply simultaneously. Replaces the even older flat layerAssetRefs[] (formatVersion 6->7 migration).

assetRef.description: asset id, see assets[] (kind:'orbLayer'), exactly 256×256px, enforced on upload. null means "show nothing (fully transparent) for this layer slot" (see ORB_LAYER_DEFAULT_ASSETS in frontend/index.html) instead of a custom image. CHANGED in Round 119 follow-up: previously null fell back to Forge's own bundled placeholder art; Tyler asked to match slay.spencerstiles.com's own Energy Counter tool instead ("Unused layers stay transparent") — every layer is optional now, upload only the ones you want. The original placeholder shape art still exists on disk and is still used, but only as 'buildFromColor' mode's internal fallback (that mode has no assetRef of its own to leave unset — see orb.mode's description).

color.description: Hex tint color, or null. null = show the image (bundled or custom) with its own native colors, no tint — this is what actually gets exported into the compiled mod too, exactly as shown. Set = the image's alpha channel becomes a CSS mask and the layer renders as a flat silhouette in that color instead — applied identically whether the underlying image is bundled default or a custom upload, so recolor and image-replace compose in the LIVE PREVIEW (see tintableVisualCss in frontend/index.html). CHANGED in Round 119: this tint IS now baked into the exported layer PNG for real (see writeCharacterArt's own comment in backend/compiler.js, and backend/lib/pngTint.js — a small, dependency-free PNG decode/tint/encode added specifically for this, after IL disassembly proved the game's own CustomEnergyCounter colors don't retint layer art at all, only the outline ring and burst VFX). The generated README.md flags this per-character when any layer has a tint set.

layerAssetRefs.description: SUPERSEDED by layers[] above (kept only so an old saved package's shape is documented; the frontend migrates this away on load and never writes it again).

backdropAssetRef.description: NEW in Round 119. asset id, see assets[] (kind:'orbBackdrop'), exactly 256×256px. This is NOT one of the 5 numbered layers[] above — it's a separate, real mechanism confirmed via full IL disassembly of Tyler's own updated TheBurdenedNewCharacter.dll: a Harmony [HarmonyPatch(typeof(NEnergyCounter),"_Ready")] postfix (class EnergyBackdrop) that inserts a TextureRect as the bottom-most (index 0) child of the orb's %Layers node at runtime — i.e. it paints UNDER everything else, including the two spin layers. null means "show nothing (fully transparent)" (ORB_BACKDROP_DEFAULT_ASSET in frontend/index.html — see orb.layers[].assetRef's own description for why this is blank rather than Forge's old opaque-shape placeholder, a Round 119 follow-up per Tyler's explicit "match the reference site" call). No color/tint parameter exists on the real patch, so unlike layers[].color there is no backdropColor field. Exported (when orb.mode !== 'default') as pack/images/packed/energy_counters/<id>_backdrop.png plus a generated Harmony patch class (see backend/templates/ForgeEnergyBackdrop.cs.template) replicating the confirmed mechanism exactly.

starColor.description: Hex tint color for the star badge, or null. Same tint mechanism as orb.layers[].color — null shows the star image (bundled or custom) with its native colors (the bundled Star.png is already a real measured cyan, #42ccff-ish, sampled from Regent's real default star icon in an earlier round); set applies a flat CSS-mask silhouette tint instead. New in formatVersion 9. CHANGED in Round 119: like orb.layers[].color, this tint is now baked into the exported star PNG for real (backend/lib/pngTint.js); the generated README.md flags this per-character when set.

poseSheetEntry.description: One uploaded sprite-sheet animation for character.poseSheets — see that field's own description for the full compile mechanism. No fixed pixel dimensions are enforced on upload (unlike every other character art slot) since a sheet's real size depends entirely on frameCount/columns — forcing a resize would corrupt the frame grid.

assetRef.description: asset id, see assets[] (kind:'poseSheet'). Uploaded as-is, no forced resize.

frameCount.description: Tyler: "the frame count should allow for as little as 1." A frameCount of 1 compiles to a single static AtlasTexture frame — a valid, real, non-animated pose.

columns.description: Grid columns for slicing the sheet — 0 (or omitted) means the legacy single-row layout (every frame side by side, sheet height IS frame height), matching Tyler's own reference TheBurdened.cs's MakeAtlasFrame default. A grid divides both axes, keeping a long animation's individual frames sharp under the game's per-image upload width cap instead of one extremely wide single-row sheet.

[VERIFIED via IL] Id/Era/EraPosition/StoryId are real abstract/virtual overrides; Title/Description/UnlockInfo resolve via LocString from the compiled epoch id, written to localization/eng/epochs.json.

name.description: Display name — compiles to this epoch's real Title LocString.

description.description: Compiles to this epoch's real Description LocString.

imageAssetRef.description: Optional. asset id, see assets[] (kind:'epochPortrait'), exactly 810×500px. [VERIFIED via IL disassembly of EpochModel::RealPortraitPath/PackedPortraitPath, cross-checked against the reference mod's .pck] On compile, written to pack/images/timeline/epoch_portraits/<this epoch's compiled id, lowercased>.png. The base game's own default Portrait getter only ever looks in a vanilla sprite atlas that never contains a mod's custom ids, so a real Harmony patch on EpochModel.Portrait (ChroniclePortrait, generated once per character with any epoch portraits) redirects it to the uploaded PNG — without an uploaded image, this epoch simply has no portrait (falls through to the vanilla atlas lookup, same as an epoch with no art in the reference mod).

era.description: [VERIFIED, exact real MegaCrit.Sts2.Core.Timeline.EpochEra enum — 26 named members, confirmed via direct fields_dump2.py read of the real installed sts2.dll, matching Tyler's 3 uploaded screenshots of the in-game Era dropdown 26-for-26.] Which point in the game's real timeline this epoch is anchored to.

unlockCardIds.description: Tyler: "if an epoch is added, at least one of the users created cards needs to be locked behind it." References this character's own cards[].id. [VERIFIED] Membership in the compiled epoch's Cards list is what the base game's own card-pool logic uses to gate these cards behind this epoch being obtained — also drives the real, auto-generated UnlockText (CreateCardUnlockText(Cards)).

epochUnlockRequirement.description: [VERIFIED via direct IL disassembly of ChronicleProgress.Evaluate in Tyler's own updated TheBurdenedNewCharacter.dll v3] A REAL, enforced condition — not just descriptive text. The reference mod compiles a generated Evaluate() method, Harmony-hooked into 4 real SaveManager/NTimelineScreen entry points, that checks this exact condition against real save-file stats and calls the real ProgressState.ObtainEpoch()/UnlockSlot() APIs. Matches Tyler's uploaded screenshot of the in-game 'Unlock requirement' dropdown's 7 options exactly.

kind.description: none = "No requirement — cards always available"; immediate = "Available immediately"; winThisCharacter = "Win runs with this character"; finishThisCharacter = "Finish runs with this character" [VERIFIED real example: TotalWins+TotalLosses>=amount]; winAnyCharacter = "Win runs with any character"; finishAnyCharacter = "Finish runs with any character"; climbFloors = "Climb floors across all runs" [VERIFIED real example: FloorsClimbed>=amount].

amount.description: Tyler: "If any option besides 'no requirement' or 'available immediately' is selected then it should pop up a number field that allows positive integers only." Required (positive integer) for every kind except none/immediate — enforced in validate.js, not here (see EPOCH_UNLOCK_REQUIREMENT_KINDS_NEEDING_AMOUNT).

cost.description: The card's fixed energy cost. NOT how X-cost cards are declared — see costsX below. [CORRECTED] An earlier round assumed the real game uses a -1 sentinel here (an STS1-style convention, never actually reflect-baselib-confirmed for STS2). Decompiling Tyler's own real, compiled, tested TheBurdenedNewCharacter.dll disproved that: its one real X-cost card (Retaliation) passes cost 0 to the base constructor, not -1 — X-cost-ness is declared by a SEPARATE override (costsX below), independent of this numeric field. cost must be exactly 0 when costsX is true (backend/validate.js) — the only value the one confirmed real example demonstrates.

costsX.description: Whether this card costs "X" (all remaining energy) — Tyler's X-cost-card ask. [VERIFIED via decompiling Tyler's own TheBurdenedNewCharacter.dll, a real compiled/tested mod] `CardModel.HasEnergyCostX` is a real, protected, virtual bool getter (default false, not abstract — confirmed by a DIFFERENT real card in the same mod, CostOfGlory, compiling fine WITHOUT overriding it); Retaliation (a real, working X-cost card in that mod) overrides it to return true. Optional; omitted/false = ordinary fixed-cost card (the common case). When true: `cost` must be 0 (see above), and this card's OnPlay effects can use "Use X" on an action's amount/hit count (actionsArray's amountIsX/hitCountIsX) to read the resolved X value via the companion real method `CardModel.ResolveEnergyXValue()` — same evidence trail, see actionsArray below.

starCost.description: Optional. Undefined/omitted = no star cost (the common case — most cards don't use stars at all). Must be 0 (or omitted) when costsStarX is true — see that field below. [VERIFIED via decompiling TheBurdenedNewCharacter.dll v3's "Star Cost Change" card, round 59, plus a direct sts2.dll metadata read] The real mechanism turned out NOT to be `CardModel.BaseStarCost` (its setter is genuinely private — CS0200 on a real dotnet build proved that back on 2026-08-27) but a DIFFERENT member, `CardModel.CanonicalStarCost` — a real, public, overridable (non-abstract) virtual int property. This compiles for real — see backend/compiler.js's generateCanonicalStarCostOverride. The companion StarsRemaining CONDITION (a different thing — the player's current live star count, not this card's own cost) is unaffected and still compiles for real as of reflect-baselib round 14 — see the conditionsArray description below.

costsStarX.description: Whether this card costs "X" stars (all remaining stars) — Tyler's round-71 ask, mirroring costsX above but for stars. [VERIFIED via decompiling Tyler's own updated TheBurdenedNewCharacter.dll, round 73] `CardModel.HasStarCostX` is a real, protected, virtual bool getter; confirmed overridden by a real working X-star-cost card ("X Star", TheBurdenedNewCharacter.Cards.XStar) in that mod — same confirmation tier as costsX/HasEnergyCostX (Retaliation). Optional; omitted/false = ordinary star cost (or none at all, the common case). When true: `starCost` must be 0 or omitted (see above).

rarity.description: Matches the real MegaCrit.Sts2.Core.Entities.Cards.CardRarity enum exactly (confirmed via reflect-baselib round 6) — 'Basic' is the real name for starting-deck cards like Strike/Defend (there is no 'Starter' or 'Special' card rarity in the real game).

target.description: Forge's own target vocabulary (shared with effect actions' targets) — compiler.js maps these onto the real MegaCrit.Sts2.Core.Entities.Cards.TargetType enum members (e.g. SingleEnemy -> AnyEnemy) at generation time.

keywords.description: Either one of the 7 real built-in MegaCrit.Sts2.Core.Entities.Cards.CardKeyword values (Exhaust/Ethereal/Innate/Retain/Unplayable/Sly/Eternal — confirmed via reflect-baselib round 1, applied via AddKeyword(CardKeyword.X)/CanonicalKeywords, a real confirmed override, round 2), or [Round 139] the `word` of one of this character's own cardKeywords[] entries — compiler.js's keywordExpr() resolves each value to the real CardKeyword.X enum member for a built-in, or to <Namespace>.Keywords.ModKeywords.X (see cardKeywords' own schema description) for a custom one; backend/validate.js accepts both against the same character's cardKeywords list. Replaced the old exhausts/innate/ethereal booleans (formatVersion 4->5 migration in frontend/index.html) so all 7 real keywords were selectable, not just 3, and no longer a closed enum now that custom keyword words are also valid. Sly ('if discarded during your turn, play it for free', per community wiki/guide docs — not reflection, behavior isn't visible to reflection, only the enum member name is) is Forge's real answer to a 'when discarded' trigger want that doesn't need a separate trigger at all.

tags.description: Forge-only organizational metadata — free-text labels the deck author assigns (e.g. "combo piece", "early game"), not a real MegaCrit/BaseLib concept (unlike keywords above, which map to the real CardKeyword enum). Powers the card section's tag-filter UI in frontend/index.html; compiler.js never reads this field, nothing here is exported into the compiled mod. NOT the same thing as gameplayTags below — that one DOES compile.

gameplayTags.description: TRUE custom tags — freeform, author-invented tag strings (e.g. "hit") that DO compile, unlike the purely organizational `tags` above. Every generated card implements a Forge-owned interface, IForgeTaggedCard (backend/templates/IForgeTaggedCard.cs.template), exposing these as a case-insensitive HashSet<string> — NOT BaseLib's real MegaCrit.Sts2.Core.Entities.Cards.CardTag enum, which reflect-baselib round 10 confirmed is a genuine, CLOSED enum (5 real members: Strike/Defend/Minion/OstyAttack/Shiv) a mod cannot add new members to at runtime, and whose extension mechanism ([CustomEnum]) has no working example anywhere reflected (not the base game, not a real installed mod) to safely replicate. Checked via a PlayedCardHasTag condition (see conditionsArray) on the OnAnyCardPlayed trigger — this is Forge's real, working answer to 'whenever a card marked X is played, this other card reacts'.

baseCardTag.description: Tyler's item 15: "tag for if card is strike or defend". Unlike gameplayTags above, this maps to the REAL, closed BaseLib/game MegaCrit.Sts2.Core.Entities.Cards.CardTag enum [CONFIRMED via reflect-baselib round 10 — exactly these 5 non-None members exist, nothing else, a mod cannot add a 6th]. Compiles to a `protected override HashSet<CardTag> CanonicalTags` on the generated card [VERIFIED override pattern — same shape as the real, reflection-confirmed CanonicalKeywords], so this card is recognized by any base-game or other-mod logic that specifically checks BaseLib's CardTag (e.g. Strike-synergy relics/powers already in the base game) — a different, narrower use case than gameplayTags, which only Forge-generated cards understand. "Strike"/"Defend" cover Tyler's literal ask; Minion/OstyAttack/Shiv are included since they're part of the same real closed enum and cost nothing extra to expose, but are mainly relevant to summon/Osty-attack/Silent-shiv-style cards. "None" (the default) omits the override entirely, same as not tagging the card at all.

artAssetRef.description: asset id, see assets[] (kind:'cardArt'). [VERIFIED, EXPORTED into the compiled mod as of round 16 — BaseLib source access + decompiling TheBurdenedNewCharacter.dll] On compile, written to pack/images/packed/card_portraits/<modIdLower>/<cardIdLower>.png and wired via the real CustomPortraitPath override, confirmed at scale: all 71 of Tyler's own real cards use this exact PNG-path override (BaseLib's Abstracts/CustomCardModel.cs confirms it's a real, publicly-overridable `virtual string?` member, Harmony-patched via a real CustomCardPortraitPngPath hook). Null/unset means no card art — the card compiles fine without one, just with no CustomPortraitPath override (falls back to whatever the base game shows for a card with no portrait).

description.description: Freeform card description text — Tyler: "an editable description box where the user can describe what the card does. If left blank, fill in the description with the closest approximation of what the card does." [VERIFIED, EXPORTED into the compiled mod as of round 16 — BaseLib source access + Tyler's own decompiled mod, description-redesign first pass, Tyler: "everything, including a first pass at description redesign"] Compiles to `public override List<(string, string)>? Localization => new CardLoc(title, description);` — reading BaseLib's real Abstracts/ILocalizationProvider.cs source directly confirms both `CustomCardModel.Localization` (a real, overridable `virtual List<(string,string)>?` member) and the real `CardLoc(string Title, string Description, ...)` record's exact implicit conversion. NO real card in the decompiled mod actually uses this path (all 71 rely on the base game auto-composing text from CanonicalVars instead — see actionsArray's CanonicalVars note), but CardLoc is BaseLib's real, confirmed mechanism for exactly this kind of freeform authored text, which is what this field is. [Round 204, Tyler: "if you make a change, the description doesn't update correctly... I want the auto-generated text to only update the preview. The editable description text box should act as an override if they put anything in it."] Left BLANK/undefined whenever the user hasn't actually typed anything — never auto-filled at save time any more (round 16 through round 203's behavior, which silently baked the auto-generated guess in here, making it look user-typed and then freezing stale on every later effect change — see autoGeneratedDescription below for where the guess now lives instead). backend/compiler.js falls back to autoGeneratedDescription, then a plain "See card effects." string, if a package reaches export with this still empty.

autoGeneratedDescription.description: [Round 204] Forge's own best-effort plain-English guess at what this card does, computed by frontend/index.html's generateCardDescription() from the card's own effects/keywords/advancedOptions and re-saved fresh every time the card editor's Done is clicked WHILE the description field is left blank (cleared back to unset the moment a real description is typed) — never touched directly by the user, never shown in the editable field itself, only ever read as compiler.js's first fallback when description is empty. Kept separate from description specifically so a real typed description always wins outright and an auto-generated guess never gets mistaken for one — see description's own note above. NOT real STS2 tooltip copy, same honesty caveat as STATUS_DESCRIPTIONS elsewhere in the app; server-side generation still doesn't exist (a package edited/imported outside the normal editor flow that never went through a save falls through to compiler.js's own plain "See card effects." string, same defense-in-depth guard as before).

effects.description: Cards compile to real CustomCardModel overrides — one per distinct trigger used. "OnPlay" -> OnPlay(...) (the original, full action support). "OnDiscard" -> AfterCardDiscarded(...) and "OnTurnEndInHand" -> OnTurnEndInHand(...), both CONFIRMED real via reflect-baselib round 9's hook-shaped-member sweep of CustomCardModel (closing the exact gap the formatVersion-5 note above referenced) — see cardEffectBlock and compiler.js:CARD_TRIGGER_HOOKS. Any trigger outside this set is rejected by the app (frontend dropdown only offers these three; backend/validate.js rejects the rest) — this used to silently compile with the effect block dropped entirely for ANY non-OnPlay trigger, caught by a real stress test (a card with a "Passive" effect block compiled clean with that block just gone, no error anywhere).

advancedOptions.description: Advanced Options — a collapsible section below the description field, Tyler's follow-up ask: "cost reduction triggers... the option to enable the card to glow when certain conditions are met... playability conditions... the ability to add effects that happen while the card is in your hand." See backend/compiler.js's own comments (costReductionTodoLines/generateGlowOverride/generateAdvancedOptionsNotes/generateCardSource) for the exact evidence trail behind each of the 4 sub-fields below. Three (costReductions, glow, whileInHand) are grounded in real evidence and compile for real: costReductions calls the real, confirmed CardEnergyCost.AddThisCombat/AddThisTurnOrUntilPlayed methods (round 24, re-verified 2026-09-07 — see costReductions' own description below); whileInHand compiles for real — as of round 195 (Tyler: "i noticed there isn't a 'whenever you play a card' trigger in here"), it supports both OnTurnEndInHand (ungated, that hook is inherently hand-only) and OnAnyCardPlayed (real per-entry this.Pile?.Type == X gating), merged into the same override method any card.effects[] block on that trigger already uses via compiler.js:whileInHandMergeLines — that same round found and fixed a real pre-existing bug where whileInHand's OnTurnEndInHand entries silently compiled to an empty, no-op override; glow compiles for real (`ShouldGlowGoldInternal` override) since decompiling Tyler's own TheBurdenedNewCharacter.dll (EnergeticAttack, Eternal) found the real mechanism. Only playability remains genuinely UNRESEARCHED — no reflect-baselib round or decompiled example has ever surfaced a CanPlay/IsPlayable-shaped override — and still compiles to nothing but a descriptive comment.

costReductions.description: "reduce the cost of this card when you play a skill or any other of the possible triggers." Each entry adjusts THIS card's own cost when one of the card's own (already-real) triggers fires — by default lowering it (the field's own name/history), or raising it when `direction` is "Increase" (round 164). [BEST EFFORT, real codegen] — round 14c's IL scan of the base game's Enlightenment.OnPlay() first found the real-NAMED CardEnergyCost.SetThisCombat(...)/SetThisTurnOrUntilPlayed(...) call (Enlightenment reduces every OTHER card in hand, not itself), but without full parameter signatures; round 24 (2026-08-30) closed that gap with a direct sts2.dll read of CardEnergyCost's real method table, confirming AddThisCombat(int amount, bool reduceOnly)/AddThisTurnOrUntilPlayed(int amount, bool reduceOnly) — the additive siblings of Enlightenment's Set-variant calls, same class, same (int, bool) shape — reached through CardModel's real public EnergyCost property. Re-verified 2026-09-07 (both CardEnergyCost's full member list AND Enlightenment's real OnPlay IL disassembled fresh) after this description itself was found stale. Compiles to `this.EnergyCost.Add<Scope>(-amount, true)` for a Decrease. See backend/compiler.js:costReductionTodoLines — including that function's own comment on the separate, one-tier-lower evidence behind Increase's `reduceOnly:false`.

trigger.description: Same 5 triggers a card's own effects[] can use (see cardEffectBlock.trigger) — Tyler's "or any other of the possible triggers."

cardTypeFilter.description: Only meaningful (and only accepted by backend/validate.js) when trigger is "OnAnyCardPlayed" — Tyler's own example, "when you play a skill." Same 5 real CardType values as card.type/conditionsArray's PlayedCardHasType. Independently optional from cardTagFilter below — when both are set they're ANDed together (compiles to a single `if (typeCheck && tagCheck)`).

cardTagFilter.description: [Round 165] Tyler: "the 'whenever any card is played' trigger should also add in a tag filter option, not just type." Only meaningful (and only accepted by backend/validate.js) when trigger is "OnAnyCardPlayed", same restriction as cardTypeFilter above. Reuses the exact same real PlayedCardHasTag condition an effect block's own "If" section already offers — Forge's own IForgeTaggedCard mechanism (a TRUE custom tag, i.e. card.gameplayTags — NOT BaseLib's closed CardTag enum), [VERIFIED via reflect-baselib round 10]. Unlike cardTypeFilter this carries no extra evidence caveat of its own — it's fully Forge-owned generated code, not dependent on any base-game internals. backend/validate.js cross-checks this against every card.gameplayTags value used anywhere in the character (case-insensitive), same as PlayedCardHasTag's own condition validation, so a typo is caught instead of silently compiling to an always-false check. Independently optional from cardTypeFilter above — when both are set they're ANDed together.

amount.description: How much to adjust this card's cost by (always a positive magnitude — `direction` below supplies the sign) — compiles to a real CardEnergyCost.Add<Scope>(±amount, reduceOnly) call, see costReductions' own description above.

direction.description: [Round 164] Tyler: "is there a way to increase the cost of the card as well?" "Decrease" (the default — every entry before this field existed behaves exactly as before) compiles to `Add<Scope>(-amount, true)`, the original [BEST EFFORT] path. "Increase" compiles to `Add<Scope>(+amount, false)` — same confirmed (int, bool) overload, no compile risk, but `reduceOnly`'s own real semantics were never independently confirmed by a decompiled sample; `false` here is inferred from Enlightenment's real `SetThisCombat(1, true)` usage (always wants cost 1, still passes true — only sensible if true means "only apply if this would actually lower the value"), so an Increase keeps that guard OFF on purpose. One evidence tier below the Decrease path — see backend/compiler.js:costReductionTodoLines's own comment for the full reasoning.

scope.description: Mirrors the two real method names found in reflect-baselib round 14c's Enlightenment evidence (SetThisCombat/SetThisTurnOrUntilPlayed) — which real STS scope the adjustment should use (compiles to the additive Add<Scope> sibling, confirmed real — see costReductions' own description above). Optional; omitted defaults to ThisCombat.

glow.description: "the option to enable the card to glow when certain conditions are met." [WIRED FOR REAL — see backend/compiler.js:generateGlowOverride] Tyler pointed at two real cards in his own TheBurdenedNewCharacter.dll (EnergeticAttack, Eternal) that both do exactly this — decompiling them found the real mechanism: `CardModel.ShouldGlowGoldInternal`, a real, non-abstract `protected virtual bool` property getter, safely overridable (a real `protected override` in both cards, not a guess). Every condition ANDed together compiles to that override's body. [2026-09-07 update] Eight condition kinds now compile to real, working code here: HasStatusStacks, HpBelowPercent, HasBlock, DebuffStacksTotal, PetIsOut, CardsPlayedThisTurn, AttacksPlayedThisTurn, and CardPositionInHand — all reached via CardModel.Owner (a real, always-accessible instance property both EnergeticAttack and Eternal call directly) instead of a cardPlay-bound local, since ShouldGlowGoldInternal is a bare property getter with no cardPlay in scope. CardPositionInHand is [VERIFIED via decompiling TheBurdenedNewCharacter.dll v3] Earthquake's own real IsPlayable override, reused here since glow and playability share the identical bare-getter shape. (HpBelowPercent/HasBlock/DebuffStacksTotal/PetIsOut were previously unguarded in this specific context — they'd generate a reference to a cardPlay-bound local that doesn't exist here, a hard C# compile failure, not a safe runtime throw; fixed by routing them through the same Owner-based resolution HasStatusStacks already used.) The remaining three kinds (EnergyRemaining/StarsRemaining/CardsInHand) have no real backing in THIS no-cardPlay context specifically — PileType.Hand.GetPile(Player).Cards etc. are real but still need a cardPlay.Player to reach — and safely fall back to ForgeActions.TodoCondition(...) per-condition, same as everywhere else those appear.

conditions.description: Same condition-kind vocabulary as an effect block's conditions, EXCEPT PlayedCardHasKeyword/PlayedCardHasTag/PlayedCardHasType — those only make sense where a cardPlay is in scope (the OnAnyCardPlayed trigger), which a glow/playability check has no equivalent of. [2026-09-07 update] HasStatusStacks, HpBelowPercent, HasBlock, DebuffStacksTotal, PetIsOut, CardsPlayedThisTurn, AttacksPlayedThisTurn, and CardPositionInHand are the eight kinds [VERIFIED] real here specifically — see conditions[].subject's own description for the one restriction (no "CardTarget" subject in this context).

playability.description: "playability conditions, so the card is only playable when your actions have met a certain criteria." [2026-09-07 — WIRED FOR REAL, see backend/compiler.js:generatePlayabilityOverride] Decompiling Tyler's own TheBurdenedNewCharacter.dll v3 found the real mechanism: CardModel.IsPlayable, a real, non-abstract `protected virtual bool` property getter — Earthquake overrides it as `PileTypeExtensions.GetPile(PileType.Hand, Owner).Cards.FirstOrDefault() == this` (leftmost card in hand) — the exact same bare-getter, no-cardPlay, Owner-reachable shape glow's ShouldGlowGoldInternal already uses (Earthquake's own glow override is literally `return this.IsPlayable;`). Every condition ANDed together compiles to that override's body via the same ctx.glowContext codegen path glow uses, so every real glow condition kind is real here too.

conditions.description: Identical real condition-kind support to card.advancedOptions.glow.properties.conditions (same eight kinds, same restrictions) — see that field's description for the full list and the CardTarget-subject exception.

whileInHand.description: "the ability to add effects that happen while the card is in your hand." Each entry is cardEffectBlock-shaped (same conditions/actions/elseActions), trigger "OnTurnEndInHand" (the closest real analog to a continuous while-in-hand hook — a TRUE continuous hook is an explicitly open research gap, see claude/feature-backlog.md group C) or, as of round 195, "OnAnyCardPlayed" ("whenever you play a card") or one of the 15 PILE_TRIGGER_HOOK_IDS ("while in a pile" — see compiler.js:PILE_TRIGGER_OWNER_GUARD). Every entry gets a `pile` field (Hand/Discard/Draw/Exhaust, default Hand) gating it to a real this.Pile?.Type == X check, EXCEPT OnTurnEndInHand, where `pile` is decorative/ignored (that hook is inherently hand-only already — round 156). OnTurnEndInHand and OnAnyCardPlayed both merge into the SAME override any card.effects[] block on that trigger already uses (backend/compiler.js:whileInHandMergeLines, round 195 — that round also fixed a real bug where OnTurnEndInHand entries here used to compile to a silently empty, no-op override, never actually reading this array at all despite this field's own prior description claiming otherwise).

heavyAttackAnimation.description: [Round 121] Only meaningful on an Attack-type card. When true, playing this card compiles a marker (the generated `IHeavyAttackCard` interface — Card.cs.template) onto the card's class so the character's own AfterCardPlayed hook (see character.poseSheets) plays the heavyAttack pose instead of the plain attack pose for this specific card. Only affects animation selection — no gameplay/damage effect. backend/validate.js rejects this on a non-Attack card (there's no "attack" pose distinction to make for a Skill/Power).

upgrades.description: One entry per unlocked upgrade tier — index 0 = Card+, 1 = Card++, 2 = Card+++, 3 = Card++++ (up to 4 tiers; see backend/compiler.js's MAX_UPGRADE_TIERS — a guess pending real confirmation of STS2's actual limit). Each entry is a diff applied at rest sites, same shape as effects plus an optional cost change, OR `null` — a `null` entry means that tier's tab exists in the editor (the user clicked "+" to add it) but it still live-mirrors the tier below it (or the base card's own effects, for index 0) rather than having diverged into its own independent data yet. Only valid on card types other than Status/Curse (no Card+ for those in real STS2) — enforced by backend/validate.js and hidden from the editor UI via isUpgradableCardType(). Replaces the older singular `upgrade` object (formatVersion 9 -> 10 migration in frontend/index.html wraps any old value into `upgrades: [oldValue]`).

starCostDelta.description: Added 2026-08-27, Tyler: "we need to add the option to modify the star cost" (on an upgrade tier, alongside the existing energy costDelta). [VERIFIED via decompiling TheBurdenedNewCharacter.dll v3's "Star Cost Change" card, round 59, re-confirmed via a second independent real card ("Star Cost", same project, later round)] CardModel.UpgradeStarCostBy(int) is a real, protected instance method — confirmed callable bare (implicit this) from a card's own OnUpgrade() override — and compiles for real: see backend/compiler.js's generateUpgradeMethod, which emits `UpgradeStarCostBy(starCostDelta)` per tier that has one set. This description used to call the mechanism unconfirmed; that was stale the moment round 59 shipped real codegen for it.

transformOnUpgrade.description: [Round 167] "the creator should allow for one card to transform into another when upgraded" (Tyler, citing his own Stomp -> Earthquake pair from TheBurdenedNewCharacter as the kind of thing he means — though direct decompilation of those two specific cards found no code link between them; this is a genuinely new capability, not a reproduction of something his mod already does). When set, this card's ONE upgrade fully replaces it with a different authored card from this same character, instead of applying a stat delta — mutually exclusive with `upgrades` (backend/validate.js rejects both being set on the same card), since a transformed card is a different CardModel instance entirely and the original's own tier list would have no meaning after it. Only valid on card types other than Status/Curse, same restriction `upgrades` already has. [BEST EFFORT] — real, solid evidence for the underlying mechanism (CardCmd.Transform/CardModel.IsTransformable/AfterTransformedFrom/AfterTransformedTo, all confirmed via direct sts2.dll IL reads), but no decompiled example of a card transforming itself on upgrade this exact way exists to confirm the full composition end-to-end (OnUpgrade is a real, confirmed-synchronous hook; CardCmd.Transform returns a Task, so it's fired without being awaited — see backend/compiler.js's generateTransformUpgradeMethod for the complete evidence trail) — see backend/compiler.js for the full writeup.

targetCardId.description: The `id` of another card defined in this same character that this card becomes on upgrade. Must reference an existing card and cannot reference this card itself — enforced by backend/validate.js.

rarity.description: Matches the real MegaCrit.Sts2.Core.Entities.Relics.RelicRarity enum exactly (confirmed via reflect-baselib round 6) — there is no 'Boss' relic rarity in the real game.

iconAssetRef.description: Optional 256×256px relic icon. [VERIFIED via direct ECMA-335 IL disassembly of the real installed sts2.dll] RelicModel.get_Icon() calls the virtual RelicModel.get_PackedIconPath() (a callvirt, confirmed via IL) and passes its return straight into Godot.ResourceLoader.Load<Texture2D>(path, null, cacheMode) — no atlas-specific gating, no .tres requirement (that generic Load call, MemberRef#562 in the raw table, was resolved by hand since il_dump.py's own typedef_or_ref_name() has a gap for a MethodSpec whose base is a MemberRef). Since PackedIconPath is virtual (unlike EpochModel.Portrait, which needed a Harmony patch in Round 203), a generated relic subclass can simply override it to point at a raw PNG — no Harmony patch needed, see backend/compiler.js's writeRelicIcon/RELIC_ICON_PREFIX.

effects.description: "OnPlay" is NOT a valid trigger here — a relic isn't "played" (see hookEffectBlock). Caught by a real stress test: a relic with trigger "OnPlay" compiled (remapped internally to AfterCardPlayed, which fires for ANY card ANYONE plays — not something intrinsic to the relic), and its DealDamage-to-SingleEnemy action compiled against a target (cardPlay.Target) borrowed from whatever card happened to trigger the hook, not a target the relic itself defines — nullable, and not what "target a single enemy with this relic" actually means.

modifiers.description: Round 20 (2026-08-25) — Group B: real AbstractModel hooks that return/gate a VALUE (a boolean decision, a numeric amount, or a set/ref parameter) instead of firing an event like effects[] above. See modifierBlock and backend/compiler.js:MODIFIER_HOOKS/generateModifierOverrides for the full per-hook evidence and codegen shape. Distinct from effects[] on purpose — these compile to a DIFFERENT override shape (e.g. `public override bool ShouldDie(Creature creature)`, not an event handler with an action list) and always call `base.<Method>(...)` first so an author's modifier composes safely with the base game and other mods instead of silently replacing their behavior.

autoClaimShopInventory.description: Round 217 — #14 claimShopInventory ("Automatically take shop items for free"). [BEST EFFORT] Optional; omitted/false = normal shop behavior (the common case). When true, compiles to a dedicated `AfterRoomEntered(AbstractRoom)` override (backend/compiler.js:generateClaimShopInventoryOverride) that, on entering a MerchantRoom, disables the top-bar Map/Deck buttons and map travel, opens/blocks the merchant UI, and purchases every stocked entry (cards, relics, potions, card removal) for free — built from a full IL trace of a real, compiled third-party mod's own async claim-shop method, with every real API member it calls independently re-confirmed via a direct ECMA-335 read of the real, installed sts2.dll. Drives live Godot UI screen nodes with hardcoded real-time waits — a genuinely different, riskier class of feature than every other modifier/effect this app generates (which only compute values or mutate data-layer lists). Compile-tested only, never played — test any relic using this in-game before trusting it in a real run.

incomingWeakBonus.description: Round 218 — #37 ("Weak's own math", defensive side). Optional whole-number percent (e.g. 56 = 0.56), omitted/0 = no effect (the common case). When set, this relic's OWNER takes extra reduced damage from Weakened attackers on top of Weak's own normal reduction — compiles to a real Harmony POSTFIX on `WeakPower.ModifyDamageMultiplicative` (backend/compiler.js:generateDebuffMultiplierSupportFile, Generated/ForgeDebuffMultiplierSupport.cs), only ever written when at least one relic sets one of these three fields. [VERIFIED via direct ECMA-335 IL trace of a real, compiled third-party mod's own DebuffMultiplierSupport.IncomingWeakBonus/.Weak() methods, cross-checked against a direct sts2.dll read of the real WeakPower.ModifyDamageMultiplicative signature this round] — see that generator's own header comment for the full evidence trail and why this app's own patch is a safer Postfix instead of the original's riskier Prefix-replaces-original approach.

vulnerableDamageBonus.description: Round 218 — #38 ("Weak's own math", offensive side). Optional whole-number percent (e.g. 32 = 0.32), omitted/0 = no effect (the common case). When set, this relic's OWNER deals extra bonus damage when attacking a Vulnerable target (self-damage excluded), on top of Vulnerable's own normal bonus — compiles to a real Harmony POSTFIX on `VulnerablePower.ModifyDamageMultiplicative`, same generator/file as incomingWeakBonus above. [VERIFIED via direct ECMA-335 IL trace of a real, compiled third-party mod's own DebuffMultiplierSupport.CrueltyBonus/.Vulnerable() methods (generalized off that mod's own CrueltyPower-specific implementation), cross-checked against a direct sts2.dll read of the real VulnerablePower.ModifyDamageMultiplicative signature this round].

amplifyWeakAndVulnerable.description: Round 218 — #39. Optional whole-number percent (e.g. 135 = 1.35x), omitted/100 = no effect (the common case). When set, multiplies how strongly BOTH Weak (while this relic's owner deals damage while weakened) and Vulnerable (while this relic's owner takes damage while vulnerable) affect that owner specifically — one field covers both directions since the real formula is symmetric (`1 + (multiplier - 1) * amplification`, applied to whichever creature actually holds the debuff). Same generator/file as incomingWeakBonus/vulnerableDamageBonus above. [VERIFIED via direct ECMA-335 IL trace of a real, compiled third-party mod's own DebuffMultiplierSupport.Amplification/.Weak()/.Vulnerable() methods].

isBuff.description: cosmetic only — green vs red styling

hideIcon.description: Round 94 — [VERIFIED against a real generated FatiguePower.cs from a different character creator tool] compiles to `protected override bool IsVisibleInternal => false;` on the generated CustomPowerModel subclass. Hides this status's icon entirely: no vanilla icon in the status row, no apply flash, and Artifact can't consume a charge from it (all three read this one flag). Independent of resourceBars below — a status can be hidden with no bar at all (pure bookkeeping), shown as a bar with the icon also visible, or hidden AND shown only as a bar. See claude/round94-hidden-status-tooltip-fix.md.

effects.description: NEW — what this mechanic actually DOES on trigger (e.g. a Poison-style "OnTurnStart -> deal damage equal to stacks"). Previously there was no way to define this at all: a mechanic compiled to a real CustomPowerModel with only its Type/StackType overrides, no behavior. Same trigger set as relics (hookEffectBlock) — "OnPlay" isn't valid here either, a power isn't "played".

modifiers.description: Round 20 — same Group B mechanism as relic.modifiers above (see that field's description and backend/compiler.js:MODIFIER_HOOKS).

enchantment.description: See the top-level `enchantments` property above for the full evidence review. Round 200 ("make this section fully functional") shape — every field below is a real, confirmed EnchantmentModel override. onApply.addKeywords/removeKeywords (see onApply below) were briefly removed in round 200, then restored in round 201 once a real, working reference enchantment proved the correct semantic: a permanent, one-way mutation applied once on enchant, never reversed on removal.

icon.description: Compiles to CustomEnchantmentModel.CustomIconPath — [VERIFIED via decompiling a real, working "STS2 Character Creator"-generated mod on Tyler's own machine] real override point.

cardFrames.description: Per-rarity card-frame art overrides applied to any card this enchantment is attached to.

modifiers.description: Numeric EnchantmentModel overrides. [VERIFIED signature] on every override below; the exact SEMANTICS of the two multiplicative fields (what they scale against) are Forge's own reasonable reading, disclosed as [BEST EFFORT] in the generated source's comments — not a guess about whether the override itself works.

perStack.description: When true, the numeric fields below scale by `* this.Amount`.

blockBonusPct.description: Compiles to EnchantBlockMultiplicative(decimal) — [VERIFIED signature, BEST EFFORT semantics] real override.

extraDamage.description: Compiles to EnchantDamageAdditive(decimal, ValueProp) — [VERIFIED] real override.

cardEffectBlock.description: One (trigger -> conditions -> actions [-> elseActions]) rule on a CARD — "If <conditions>, then <actions>, else <elseActions>" (Tyler's request; see elseActions below). "OnPlay" has full action support (real player/target Creature binding, confirmed since round 5). "OnDiscard"/"OnTurnEndInHand" are real, confirmed-compiling triggers (round 9) but their real hook signatures don't expose a confirmed player/target Creature yet, so their actions currently compile to a runtime NotImplementedException (ForgeActions.Todo(...)) rather than real behavior, same pattern already used for several relic/mechanic hook triggers — see compiler.js:CARD_TRIGGER_HOOKS. "OnAnyCardPlayed" is also real (AfterCardPlayed, confirmed since round 2 but not wired up until now) and — unlike OnDiscard/OnTurnEndInHand — has FULL real action support, same CardPlay binding as OnPlay: it fires whenever ANY card is played by anyone (including this card's own play), which is the real mechanism for a 'whenever a card with X is played, this reacts' synergy. Pair it with a PlayedCardHasKeyword condition (real CardKeyword values only) or a PlayedCardHasTag condition (TRUE custom tags — see card.gameplayTags and conditionsArray) to scope it to specific cards. "OnRetained" [Round 95, VERIFIED via decompiling TheBurdenedNewCharacter.dll's real, shipped PatientStrike.cs AND TrainedAssault.cs — both override AfterFlush(PlayerChoiceContext, Player, IReadOnlyCollection<CardModel> flushedCards, IReadOnlyCollection<CardModel> retainedCards), gated identically on `player == base.Owner && retainedCards.Contains(this)`] fires once at end of turn if THIS card was retained by its own owner — same real fgPlayer/fgPet binding as OnDiscard/OnTurnEndInHand (via this.Owner), no real target Creature (nothing is targeted by being retained).

elseActions.description: OPTIONAL — runs INSTEAD of `actions` when `conditions` evaluates false (compiler.js emits a real C# `else` block). Only meaningful (and only accepted by backend/validate.js) when `conditions` has at least one entry — an else with nothing to be the opposite of is rejected. A character can stack several effect blocks under the same trigger (Tyler's 'multiple if/else statements' ask) — e.g. one block checking Strength with its own else, and a second, independent block checking Dexterity right after it, both under OnPlay.

hookEffectBlock.description: One (trigger -> conditions -> actions [-> elseActions]) rule on a RELIC or MECHANIC — both are hook-driven (react to combat events) rather than "played" like a card, so "OnPlay" is excluded here on purpose. "OnAnyCardPlayed" (AfterCardPlayed) IS included — a relic/power isn't itself played, but it can react to any card being played, with full real target binding (see compiler.js:TRIGGER_HOOKS). Pair it with PlayedCardHasKeyword or PlayedCardHasTag (see conditionsArray) the same way a card can, e.g. a relic that reacts whenever a card tagged "hit" is played by anyone. See cardEffectBlock.elseActions above — same optional if/else shape, same trigger set for OnAnyCardPlayed.

modifierBlock.description: Round 20 (2026-08-25) — Group B: one (hook -> conditions -> value) rule on a RELIC or MECHANIC, gating a real value-returning AbstractModel hook (a boolean gate, a numeric modifier, or a gate+modifier) instead of an event-style trigger. Every shape's generated override calls the real `base.<Method>(...)` first (or falls through to it when conditions don't match) so a Forge-authored modifier composes safely alongside the base game and other mods instead of silently replacing their behavior — see each shape's own codegen in generateModifierOverrides.

gateValue.description: Used only by the 8 'gate' hooks (ShouldPlay/ShouldDie/ShouldClearBlock/ShouldDraw/ShouldAllowHitting/ShouldPlayerResetEnergy/ShouldPayExcessEnergyCostWithStars/ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDeath) — the value to force-return when `conditions` match. numericMode.description: Used only by the 17 'numeric' hooks. 4 of them (ModifyBlockAdditive/ModifyPowerAmountGivenAdditive — Add; ModifyBlockMultiplicative — Multiply; ModifyDamageAdditive — Add; ModifyDamageMultiplicative — Multiply) have this LOCKED by backend/compiler.js to match what the hook's own real name already promises (using the other operation there would contradict what the hook's name tells the base game/other mods it does) — the frontend disables this field for those and shows the locked operation instead. The other 13 accept any of the 3; omitted defaults to "Add".

numericValue.description: Used only by the 17 'numeric' hooks — the amount to Add/Multiply/Set. Applied on top of `base.<Method>(...)`'s own real return value (so this composes with the base game/other mods), only when `conditions` match.

redirectMode.description: [Round 208] Used only by ModifyUnblockedDamageTarget — redirects a hit to a random ally or enemy OF THE ATTACKER (dealer) instead of its original target, when conditions match. Compiles to a real Creature.CombatState.GetTeammatesOf/GetOpponentsOf(Creature) call (both confirmed real, public, abstract ICombatState interface members via direct sts2.dll read); falls back to the original target when the candidate pool is empty (e.g. no allies in a solo fight).

items.description: Every kind requires "kind" plus its own fields: HasStatusStacks/HpBelowPercent/EnergyRemaining/StarsRemaining/CardsInHand/CardsPlayedThisTurn use comparator+value; PlayedCardHasKeyword uses `keyword` instead (a boolean has/has-not check on the card that triggered an OnAnyCardPlayed hook, not a numeric threshold), PlayedCardHasTag uses `tag` (same shape, but a freeform string instead of a fixed enum — see card.gameplayTags), and PlayedCardHasType uses `cardType` (same shape, one of the 5 real CardType values — see card.type) — all three only validate on the OnAnyCardPlayed trigger — see backend/validate.js. CardsPlayedThisTurn [VERIFIED via decompiling TheBurdenedNewCharacter.dll's Eternal] uses comparator+value like the others, no subject — counts how many cards this card's own owner has finished playing so far this turn (real CombatManager.Instance.History.CardPlaysFinished walk, no cardPlay local needed — valid on every trigger AND inside glow/playability). Originally shipped as a fixed "< 1" check named FirstCardPlayedThisTurn; generalized into this real comparator+value form per Tyler's follow-up ("the glow condition should instead check if cards played this turn are <= an amount") — an old saved FirstCardPlayedThisTurn condition migrates to CardsPlayedThisTurn with comparator "lte"/value 0 (formatVersion 13->14 in frontend/index.html), the exact equivalent of the old fixed check. EnergyRemaining/StarsRemaining [VERIFIED via reflect-baselib round 14a/14b]: Player.PlayerCombatState.Energy/.Stars are real, live, get/set int counts, reached via `cardPlay.Player` — compiles for real wherever a card's own effects run (OnPlay, OnAnyCardPlayed) and on a relic/mechanic's OnAnyCardPlayed hook. The one narrow exception is a relic/mechanic's OnTakeDamage hook, whose real params have no CardPlay to reach the player through — still falls back to ForgeActions.TodoCondition there specifically — see backend/compiler.js. DamageBrokeBlock (added 2026-08-26, Tyler's "Flick" lead — [VERIFIED via decompiling TheBurdenedNewCharacter.dll's Flick, same DLL as Eternal/Retaliation above]) takes NO comparator/value/subject at all — a plain boolean check on whether the LAST damage this card dealt broke its target's block (real CombatManager.Instance.History.Entries.OfType<DamageReceivedEntry>() walk, matching entries by CardSource == this and reading Result.WasBlockBroken — see backend/compiler.js:conditionToCSharp's DamageBrokeBlock case for the full writeup). Only valid on the OnPlay trigger, and only meaningful placed in a second effect block right after a Deal Damage effect on that same trigger — per Tyler's own instruction ("if this damage broke their block is a conditional to the stun effect and not directly tied to it"), this is a SEPARATE condition gating a later action (e.g. Stun Enemy), not a field bundled into the Deal Damage action itself. CardsInHand (2026-08-27, round 16 — BaseLib source access) is now [BEST EFFORT] real codegen, same tier and same restriction as EnergyRemaining/StarsRemaining above — MegaCrit.Sts2.Core.Models.PileType.Hand.GetPile(cardPlay.Player).Cards.Count() is a real, confirmed hand-pile access, reached the same way through cardPlay.Player.

kind.description: 2026-08-27 condition-kind expansion round (Tyler's FollowUp1-4 screenshots + "lets go through all of the conditions expansions") — 9 new kinds added after an exhaustive research pass (BaseLib source, sts2.dll/sts2.xml direct read, both real decompiled mods). Every one below has a confirmed real backing member; nothing here is a placeholder. "HasBlock" [VERIFIED via sts2.dll — Creature.Block] and "DebuffStacksTotal" [VERIFIED via sts2.dll — Creature.Powers + PowerType.Debuff] both use subject+comparator+value, same subject mechanism as HpBelowPercent (see subject below, and backend/compiler.js:SUBJECT_CAPABLE_CONDITION_KINDS). "PetIsOut" [VERIFIED via sts2.dll — Creature.Pets] uses subject only, boolean (does this creature have a pet out), same no-comparator shape as DamageBrokeBlock. "HandCardTypeCheck" [VERIFIED via sts2.dll — PileType.Hand.GetPile(Player).Cards] uses `mode` (Any/All) + `cardType` (reusing PlayedCardHasType's own cardType enum), cardPlayBound only (same restriction as CardsInHand). "AttacksPlayedThisTurn" [VERIFIED via sts2.dll — extends the same real CombatManager.Instance.History.CardPlaysFinished walk CardsPlayedThisTurn already uses, filtered to CardType.Attack] uses comparator+value, no subject, valid on every trigger AND inside glow/playability just like CardsPlayedThisTurn. "OrbSlotCount" [VERIFIED via sts2.dll — Player.BaseOrbSlotCount] uses comparator+value, cardPlayBound only. "EnemyIntent" [VERIFIED via sts2.dll — Monster.NextMove.Intents] uses `intentKind` (Attack/Defend only — the only two Intent subclasses confirmed via sts2.dll at this pass), cardPlayBound only, boolean (no comparator/value). "HasSpecificRelic" [VERIFIED — reuses the same real Player.Relics + ModelDb-class-identity pattern startingRelicId already uses] uses `relicRef` (a relic id from this character's own relics[]), cardPlayBound only, boolean. "NoCopiesOfCardInHand" [VERIFIED — same PileType.Hand.GetPile access as HandCardTypeCheck, same cardClassById identity pattern as HasSpecificRelic] uses `cardRef` (a card id from this character's own cards[]), cardPlayBound only, boolean. See claude/toolchain-findings.md's 2026-08-27 section for the full evidence trail on every kind above. [2026-09-07 update] CardPositionInHand [VERIFIED via decompiling TheBurdenedNewCharacter.dll v3 — Earthquake's real IsPlayable override: PileTypeExtensions.GetPile(PileType.Hand, Owner).Cards.FirstOrDefault() == this] checks whether THIS card sits at a specific position in the player's hand, uses `edge` (Left/Right) + `position` (1-based int; 1 = the edge card itself), no comparator/value. Real in card.advancedOptions.glow and card.advancedOptions.playability (checks THIS card's LIVE hand position), and — as of round 54 — on a card's own OnPlay and OnAnyCardPlayed triggers too (requiresTrigger: 'glowOrPlayabilityOrCardPlayBound', see backend/validate.js and frontend/index.html:conditionKindAllowedForTrigger), which instead check a CAPTURED snapshot: [2026-09-08 round 53, VERIFIED via decompiling sts2.dll's CardModel.OnPlayWrapper/CardPileCmd.AddDuringManualCardPlay] a live check is unconditionally false on OnPlay/OnAnyCardPlayed since the card has already left the Hand pile by the time either trigger's conditions evaluate — but [2026-09-08 round 54, VERIFIED via decompiling TheBurdenedNewCharacter.dll v4] Tyler's own updated Strike card proves the real fix: a Harmony PREFIX patch on CardModel.OnPlayWrapper (his ModHandPositionPatch) captures the position BEFORE that removal happens. Generated/ForgeHandPositionTracker.cs reimplements that mechanism generically (see Generated/IForgeHandPosition.cs) so OnPlay (checks `this`) and OnAnyCardPlayed (checks `cardPlay.Card`, same pattern PlayedCardHasTag/Keyword/Type use) both compile for real now. [2026-09-08 round 56, VERIFIED via decompiling sts2.dll's CardCmd.DiscardAndDraw/CombatManager.DoTurnEndCards] OnDiscard and OnTurnEndInHand have the exact same "already gone from Hand by the time the real hook fires" problem OnPlay used to have (Discard moves the card into the Discard pile before Hook.AfterCardDiscarded; turn-end processing moves it into the Play pile, via AddTurnEndCardToPlayPileWithDelay, before CardModel.OnTurnEndInHandWrapper) — so two more Harmony prefixes, Generated/ForgeHandPositionDiscardTracker.cs and Generated/ForgeHandPositionTurnEndTracker.cs, now capture the position before THOSE removals too, the same technique round 54 proved for OnPlay. All 4 of a card's own triggers (OnPlay/OnDiscard/OnTurnEndInHand/OnAnyCardPlayed) are real now (requiresTrigger: 'glowOrPlayabilityOrCardTrigger', renamed from 'glowOrPlayabilityOrCardPlayBound' since it's no longer just the 2 card-play-bound triggers). A relic/mechanic modifier hook still has no card of its own to check, so it's still excluded. This round also gave the row a dedicated 'This card'/'That card' subject-style slot in the UI (see frontend/index.html:cardPositionInHandSubject) instead of folding the subject into the kind dropdown's own label text. See claude/round52-card-position-and-playability.md, claude/round53-hand-position-pile-timing.md, claude/round54-hand-position-bonus-damage.md, claude/round55-hand-position-wording.md, and claude/round56-hand-position-targets.md for the full evidence trail.

statusKind.description: used only by kind == HasStatusStacks — whether `builtinStatus` (a real, built-in game status) or `statusRef` (one of this character's own mechanics) is the status being checked. Mirrors the existing ApplyStatus (vanilla) vs. ApplyCustomStatus (custom) action-side split — added per Tyler's follow-up: "the condition that checks for statuses should work on both vanilla as well as custom statuses. Currently it only works for custom." Optional; omitted/undefined is read as "custom" — the only kind this condition supported before this field existed, so packages saved before this round keep compiling to the exact same behavior.

statusRef.description: mechanic id, used by kind == HasStatusStacks when statusKind == "custom" (or omitted, for backward compatibility).

builtinStatus.description: a real built-in status name (see actionsArray's builtinStatuses for the full 244-entry list — same BUILTIN_POWER_CLASS_MAP), used by kind == HasStatusStacks when statusKind == "vanilla". Compiles to ForgeActions.GetStatusStacks<T>() with T resolved from BUILTIN_POWER_CLASS_MAP, exactly like the ApplyStatus/RemoveStatus actions already do — see backend/compiler.js:conditionToCSharp's HasStatusStacks case.
