ref.description: the built-in status name or mechanic id, per `kind` above.

amount.description: only meaningful when the action's `mode` is "Add" (Remove never used an amount, matching the old RemoveStatus/RemoveCustomStatus behavior) — stacks to apply for THIS entry specifically. Missing/undefined falls back to 1 (backend/compiler.js:resolveStatusEntryAmountExpr), same fallback chain the old statusAmounts/refAmounts maps used.

statusEntries.description: type == "ModifyStatus" only — required (non-empty). Replaces the old separate builtinStatuses[]/statusRefs[] + statusAmounts{}/refAmounts{} — ONE combined list (Tyler: "we can use the combined vanilla+custom status list so we can get rid of the custom options") so a single ModifyStatus action can add/remove a mix of real statuses and custom mechanics together (e.g. Vulnerable + your own "Ember" mechanic in one action), each entry with its own amount when adding. One ForgeActions call is generated per entry, sharing this action's target and `mode`.

amount.description: used directly by single-target action types (DealDamage, GainBlock, ModifyHp, DrawCard, ModifyGold, DiscardCard, ExhaustCard, CreateCard, ModifyOrbSlots). As of round 160, ModifyEnergy/ModifyOrbSlots's `amount` is always a positive magnitude — like ModifyHp/ModifyGold, the sibling `mode` field (not the amount's sign) decides direction (see `mode`/`type` above). [VERIFIED via decompiling Tyler's own TheBurdenedNewCharacter.dll, a real compiled/tested mod] `CardModel.ResolveEnergyXValue()` is a real, concrete, zero-argument instance method returning int, confirmed used exactly this way by a real working card (Retaliation) to scale a real AttackCommand call. Only valid on a card whose own `costsX` is true, inside that SAME card's own OnPlay effect block (the only trigger the confirmed example uses it in — enforced in backend/validate.js). Takes priority over amount/amountScalesWith* when set; for ApplyStatus/ApplyCustomStatus with multiple selected statuses, X is used for every selected entry in the action (no per-entry override). Mutually exclusive with amountIsStarX below (backend/validate.js rejects both true at once) — they're alternate sources for the same amount, not stackable.

amountIsStarX.description: Round 74, Tyler: "lets go ahead and build that in." amountScalesWithStatusKind.description: used only when amountScalesWithStatus or amountScalesWithBuiltinStatus is set — whether the scaling status is one of this character's own mechanics ("custom") or a real built-in game status ("vanilla", e.g. Poison). Optional; omitted/undefined is read as "custom" — the only kind this field supported before Tyler's follow-up ("status needs a 'do this thing equal to the number of stacks of the status I have' like poison") added vanilla support.

amountScalesWithStatus.description: mechanic id — amount becomes 'X per stack' of this custom mechanic, whose stacks are read off amountScalesWithSubject (default Self, the acting player — the only subject this ever checked before that field existed), if amountScalesWithStatusKind is "custom" (or omitted).

amountScalesWithBuiltinStatus.description: a real built-in status name (see actionsArray's builtinStatuses for the full list) — amount becomes 'X per stack' of this real status, whose stacks are read off amountScalesWithSubject (default Self), if amountScalesWithStatusKind is "vanilla". E.g. amount=1 with this set to "Poison" and subject Self means "deal damage equal to your own Poison stacks" — Tyler's original ask.

amountScalesWithSubject.description: used only when per-stack scaling is on (amountScalesWithStatus/amountScalesWithBuiltinStatus set) — whose stacks of that status/mechanic to count. trigger.description: Added 2026-08-27, Tyler: "add an optional 'follow up' below each added 'then' section on card effects... like 'deal 6 damage to target' follow up -> 'if this damage kills/breaks block/any other triggers' [do something else]". "BrokeBlock" [VERIFIED via decompiling TheBurdenedNewCharacter.dll's "Flick"] reads the SAME real DamageResult.WasBlockBroken field the existing standalone "DamageBrokeBlock" condition kind already uses (see conditionsArray/CONDITION_KINDS), via the identical CombatManager.Instance.History.Entries.OfType<DamageReceivedEntry>() walk. "KilledTarget" [BEST EFFORT] reads DamageResult.WasTargetKilled — a real field on the exact same DamageResult type (confirmed via TemperedStrength's real usage, which reads it through AttackCommand.Results instead of the History walk; both access paths return the identical DamageResult type, confirmed independently via BaseLib's own AttackCommandExtensions.ExecuteAndCheckFatal helper — so reading WasTargetKilled through the History-walk path specifically is a same-type, different-field extension, not directly observed in exactly this form, hence BEST EFFORT rather than VERIFIED). "FullyBlocked" and "UnblockedAmount" added 2026-08-27 in the condition-kind expansion round — both [VERIFIED via sts2.dll], reading the same DamageResult record's WasFullyBlocked and UnblockedDamage fields respectively, through the identical History-walk access path as BrokeBlock/DamageBrokeBlock. "UnblockedAmount" additionally needs `comparator`+`value` below (e.g. "unblocked damage >= 10"); the other three triggers are plain booleans and ignore comparator/value. Unlike the standalone DamageBrokeBlock condition (which requires the author to manually place a second effect block immediately after a Deal Damage effect, with no way for Forge to check they did), nesting this directly under the Deal Damage action that causes it removes that whole misuse class — the codegen always emits the check immediately after this exact action, in the same method body, so there's no separate placement discipline required. Valid on any trigger this Deal Damage action itself can be used on — the underlying History walk needs no cardPlay-bound context (matches DamageBrokeBlock's own "no ctx branching needed" reasoning).

comparator.description: used only when `trigger` above is "UnblockedAmount" — compares DamageResult.UnblockedDamage against `value` below. Ignored (and not required) for the other 3 boolean triggers.

value.description: used only when `trigger` above is "UnblockedAmount" — the threshold `comparator` compares DamageResult.UnblockedDamage against. Ignored (and not required) for the other 3 boolean triggers.

actions.description: The action(s) to run only when `trigger` above was true for the damage this Deal Damage action just dealt. Same actionsArray shape as any other action list (effect.actions/elseActions) — can itself contain another DealDamage action with its own nested followUp, though that's an unusual, untested combination.

followUp.description: DealDamage only. Optional — Tyler's "follow up" ask: an action (or actions) that only run if this specific damage instance broke the target's block or killed the target. Omitted/absent = no follow-up (unchanged behavior). See `trigger` above for the full evidence writeup.
